cells.value: Ask (default) prompts for anything not already allowed. [ui] permission_mode takes default, ask, auto or always-approve. dontAsk silently denies anything without an explicit allow rule (headless, CI). Plan mode's file-edit gate is independent of the permission mode (ask, auto, or always-approve).

--always-approve (alias --yolo) auto-approves all tool executions. Always-approve skips permission prompts for tool calls, but deny rules and PreToolUse hooks still apply. disable_bypass_permissions_mode = true under [ui] turns always-approve off across the deployment.
Auto mode uses a classifier to auto-approve safe tools; dangerous ones may still prompt, and deny rules and hooks still apply. Toggle with /auto or Shift+Tab when the feature is enabled.
cells.limitation: Only safe tools are auto-approved; 'dangerous ones may still prompt', and Auto is toggled 'when the feature is enabled'.

cells.value: [subagents.models] maps each subagent to a model id, giving per-subagent model routing.
At most 50 scheduled tasks can be active at once. Loops expire after 7 days; the interval accepts Ns (minimum 60), Nm, Nh and Nd.
cells.limitation: The cap is stated for scheduled tasks only: 'at most 50 scheduled tasks can be active at once'; the quote gives no limit on concurrent agents or sessions.

cells.value: Subagents spawn independent child sessions that handle tasks in parallel. Workflows orchestrate a bounded set of background subagents (fan out, verify, return a result) and are on by default. Subagents can request worktree isolation when the parent delegates parallel work.
cells.limitation: GROK_SUBAGENTS ('Enable subagents / the task tool') defaults to 0 (E-grok-build-00066), while Workflows, which use subagents, are 'on by default' (E-grok-build-00329); these quotes do not settle whether subagents are enabled out of the box.

cells.value: Grok runs commands, subagents and monitors in the background while the conversation continues. Ctrl+B sends the running command to the background; /tasks lists background tasks, subagents and scheduled tasks. [toolset.bash] auto_background_on_timeout (default true) backgrounds a command on timeout.
Ctrl+M picks a model when the prompt is not focused. /model <name> (alias /m) switches the active model. [models] hidden_models hides models from the picker while they stay usable via -m.

-m, --model <MODEL> sets the model ID to use. GROK_DEFAULT_MODEL sets the session default model (same idea as -m / --model). [ui] fork_secondary_model sets the model for the secondary agent when forking.

[model.<id>] defines custom/BYOK models (OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic Messages); env_key is preferred over api_key. Any custom model can be added in ~/.grok/config.toml. Credentials resolve per model: model.api_key > model.env_key > active session token > XAI_API_KEY.
grok-4.7 is available directly on the xAI API and in us-east-1, us-west-2 and us-central-1. [models] disabled_models removes models from the catalog and wins over hidden_models.
Grok 4.7 supports reasoning efforts low, medium, high and xhigh. [models] default_reasoning_effort sets the default reasoning effort for the default model.
cells.limitation: Levels are given for Grok 4.7 only; default_reasoning_effort takes an 'effort level if supported', and the cited quotes do not state a default value.

cells.value: /effort sets reasoning effort for the current model. [models] default_reasoning_effort sets the default for the default model. Per-model supports_reasoning_effort / reasoning_effort give reasoning controls when the model supports them.
Per-model supports_reasoning_effort / reasoning_effort provide reasoning controls when the model supports them. Grok 4.7 supports reasoning efforts low, medium, high and xhigh.
cells.limitation: Controls apply only 'when supported' by the model; the cited quotes list levels for Grok 4.7 only.

cells.value: GROK_SHOW_THINKING_BLOCKS (default 1) shows thinking/reasoning blocks in the TUI; [ui] show_thinking_blocks (default true) shows them while streaming. [ui] max_thoughts_width (40-500, default 120) sets the thoughts panel column width.
cells.limitation: Cited quotes cover only whether thinking/reasoning blocks are shown and the thoughts panel width; none states a token budget.

cells.value: Shift+Tab cycles Normal, Plan, Auto (when available) and Always-approve. The [ui] permission_mode setting accepts default, ask, auto or always-approve.

Shift+Tab cycles Normal, Plan, Auto (when available) and Always-approve. /plan [description] enters plan mode (active on the next prompt). /auto toggles auto mode when the feature is enabled. /always-approve or grok --always-approve enters always-approve.

In plan mode only the session plan file can be edited until you approve, independent of permission mode; the plan review is not skipped under auto or always-approve. The agent can enter plan mode on its own; leave with Shift+Tab when idle or q on the approval screen.
cells.limitation: Plan mode gates edit tools, not the shell — bash can still write via redirection. Reads, bash, and MCP still follow permission mode.

cells.value: Auto uses a classifier to auto-approve safe tools; dangerous ones may still prompt. Always-approve skips permission prompts for tool calls (/always-approve, Shift+Tab or grok --always-approve). Deny rules and hooks still apply; auto and always-approve do not skip plan review.
GROK_WRITE_FILE (default 1) set to 0 disables the write tool, described as for read-only sessions.
cells.limitation: Env var disables the `write` tool ("read-only sessions"); the quote does not describe a named read-only mode or cover other file-changing tools.

cells.value: [ui] permission_mode takes default, ask, auto or always-approve as the default tool-permission behavior. Legacy keys approval_mode and yolo = true still work; permission_mode wins when more than one is set. Plan mode stays on until you approve or quit.
cells.limitation: Default in user config only (`~/.grok/config.toml` or managed/requirements — not project `.grok/config.toml`).
